claims.text: The starting catalyst is a near-equiatomic multi-principal-element alloy with minimal platinum-group-metal content.
The intervention is to add approximately 5 atomic percent cerium during synthesis.
Incorporating a dispersed ceria phase is equivalent to doping the alloy with cerium.
Cerium addition will cause cerium-rich oxide clusters or thin surface layers to form and segregate during processing or aging.
The cerium-rich surface domains will remain stable during long-term catalyst operation.
Cerium-rich domains will increase oxygen mobility at the catalyst surface.
Cerium-rich domains will enhance surface redox cycling.
Enhanced oxygen mobility and redox cycling will lower reaction-energy barriers for CO oxidation.
Enhanced oxygen mobility and redox cycling will lower reaction-energy barriers for hydrocarbon oxidation.
Cerium-rich domains will improve resistance to H2O poisoning by adsorbing or blocking the poisoning species.
Cerium-rich domains will improve resistance to NO poisoning by adsorbing or blocking the poisoning species.
Cerium-rich domains will hinder sintering or agglomeration of active metal particles.
Suppressing sintering or agglomeration will improve catalyst lifetime durability.
Relative to the unmodified catalyst, the cerium-modified catalyst will have higher CO and hydrocarbon oxidation activity at temperatures at or below 150 °C.
Relative to the unmodified catalyst, the cerium-modified catalyst will experience less activity loss in the presence of H2O and NO.
Relative to the unmodified catalyst, the cerium-modified catalyst will exhibit less performance degradation during extended accelerated aging.
The intervention can provide these benefits without increasing platinum-group-metal usage.
The predicted benefits apply to transient low-temperature exhaust containing CO, hydrocarbons, H2O, and NO and to accelerated aging intended to simulate lifetime mileage.

contradictions.description: The conditions include operation at temperatures at or below 150 °C, whereas the boundary restricts the prediction to temperatures strictly below 150 °C.
